module.name: Collatz and integer S-units: small source-backed base

source.scope: Six curated concepts; no inference edges; no Collatz proof or disproof.

concepts.name: Shortcut Collatz map
concepts.statement: For positive integers, T(n)=n/2 when n is even, and T(n)=(3n+1)/2 when n is odd.
concepts.description: For positive integers, T(n)=n/2 when n is even, and T(n)=(3n+1)/2 when n is odd.

source.note: Source-backed curator paraphrase; not locally formalized or compiler verified.

concepts.name: Wave and wave-minimum
concepts.statement: For an odd start n>=3, a wave begins at a local minimum mu, has k>=2 successive odd entries including mu, and ends at the next even iterate T^k(mu).
concepts.description: For an odd start n>=3, a wave begins at a local minimum mu, has k>=2 successive odd entries including mu, and ends at the next even iterate T^k(mu).

source.note: Source-backed curator paraphrase; not locally formalized or compiler verified.

concepts.name: Primes generated by a wave
concepts.statement: Prm(mu) consists of 3 and the prime divisors of mu+1 and T^s(mu) for 1<=s<=k, for a wave of height k.
concepts.description: Prm(mu) consists of 3 and the prime divisors of mu+1 and T^s(mu) for 1<=s<=k, for a wave of height k.

concepts.name: Conditional infinitude of generated primes
concepts.statement: If an odd n>=3 has a divergent T-trajectory and all its waves have heights bounded by one M>=2, the union of their Prm(mu) sets is infinite.
concepts.description: If an odd n>=3 has a divergent T-trajectory and all its waves have heights bounded by one M>=2, the union of their Prm(mu) sets is infinite.
hypotheses: One uniform integer M>=2 bounds every wave height

concepts.name: Integer S-units
concepts.statement: For a finite prime set S, a nonzero integer is an integer S-unit when every prime divisor of its absolute value belongs to S.
concepts.description: For a finite prime set S, a nonzero integer is an integer S-unit when every prime divisor of its absolute value belongs to S.
hypotheses: S is a finite set of primes

concepts.name: Natural p-adic valuation
concepts.statement: For p!=1 and n>0, padicValNat p n is the largest k with p^k dividing n. Mathlib returns zero when n=0 or p=1.
